runs.t: By the end of class, you can do these six things.
I can give instructions in order.
I can ask How do I…? What do I do next?
I can give a warning with Don't….
I can read a medicine label (invented).
I can write 4 steps for a task I know.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: first, next, then, after that, finally. Goal 2: follow spoken instructions and number the steps. Goal 3: How do I…? What do I do next? What do I do after that?
Goal 4: Don't… and Don't forget to… Goal 5: read a medicine label (invented) and answer questions about it. Goal 6: write 4 steps for a task they know.
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check. It is not a test grade.

Listening script (the audio is coming soon; until then, read it aloud with a volunteer at a normal, friendly speed):
Narrator: Lesson ten. Listening. Maria is a new worker at a supermarket. Her coworker Tom is teaching her to use a machine. Listen.
Tom: Hi, Maria. Welcome to the team! Today I'm going to show you the floor cleaning machine. It's easy.
Maria: Great. How do I start?
Tom: First, put on your safety goggles. Then, fill the tank with water.
Maria: Why do I need goggles?
Tom: Because the detergent can hurt your eyes. Next, add one cup of detergent. Not more!
Maria: One cup. Got it. What do I do after that?
Tom: After that, plug it in and turn it on. A green light comes on.
Maria: And then I just push it?
Tom: Right. Push it slowly. Don't leave it alone when it's on.
Maria: What do I do when I finish?
Tom: Finally, turn it off, unplug it, and empty the tank.
Maria: Thanks, Tom. Can I try it now?
Tom: Sure. Press the start button, and let's go. I'll walk with you.
Narrator: That's the end of the listening.

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: Teach Me in Four Steps · 12 min. Pairs.
How it works: the Talk Time page has 4 strips. In each strip, the 4 pictures (A–D) are not in order. A chooses a strip, finds the right order (writes it under the strip), and teaches B with sequence words. B mimes each step and asks What do I do next? Then switch with a new strip. Each click shows the next step.
Model with one learner (1 min): strip 1: "First, turn on the water." (point to B) "Next, use soap." (D) … The learner mimes.
Rounds (8 min): about 2 minutes per strip; each pair does all 4 strips if there is time. Walk around and listen for the sequence words. Finish (2 min): ask 2 pairs to teach one strip to the class.
The right order: strip 1 (washing hands) B, D, A, C • strip 2 (coffee) C, A, D, B • strip 3 (a photo) D, B, C, A • strip 4 (parking) A, D, B, C. The sentences learners say will vary.
Mixed levels: stronger learners add a Don't… warning to each strip. If behind: 2 strips only.
Lesson plan: Step 5; Talk Time page; Answer key.

Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: two steps for a task with sequence words (First, open the app. Then, type your password.), and one warning with Don't and a reason with because or so (Don't open the door, because the water is hot.). Collect at the door.

runs.t: I can give instructions in order.
I can ask How do I…? What do I do next?
I can read a medicine label.
A. Listen to the teacher. Circle a or b.
a. plug it in → turn it on   b. turn it on → plug it in
a. Open the door.   b. Don't open the door.
a. press START   b. press STOP
a. This is the first step.   b. This is the last step.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle a or b. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "First, plug it in. Then, turn it on." (a) • 2 "Don't open the door." (b) • 3 "After that, press START." (a) • 4 "Finally, take your card." (b)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 First, 2 Press, 3 Don't, 4 Finally. C: answers will vary (for example First, open the app. Next, type your password. Then, press LOG IN. / Don't forget to take your receipt.).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help hearing the steps (A) and with the forms (B, C).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 12). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 12 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
